MODERN STANDARD ARABICFROM THE BEGINNING

01 / WHO IT IS FOR

A starting point
for beginners.

This proposed programme is designed for adults with little or no Arabic knowledge who want an introduction explained in English.

The focus is Modern Standard Arabic. Regional dialect teaching is outside this programme’s scope.

02 / PROGRAMME OUTLINE

Four weeks.
One step at a time.

01

WEEK 1

Meet the letters and sounds

Explore Arabic reading direction, letter shapes, and introductory pronunciation practice.

02

WEEK 2

Begin a conversation

Practise greetings and simple introductions.

03

WEEK 3

Build familiarity

Explore familiar words and short expressions through small practice activities.

04

WEEK 4

Bring it together

Revisit the foundations through guided reading, listening, and speaking practice.

03 / SAMPLE LESSON

Begin with hello.

YOUR FIRST WORD

مَرْحَبًا

marḥaban

Hello

Recording transcript: مَرْحَبًا — Hello.

  1. Look at the Arabic word.
  2. Play the pronunciation recording.
  3. Pause and try saying it aloud.
  4. Listen again and compare.

The English transliteration is a reading aid. Use the recording to hear the Arabic pronunciation.

Pronunciation audio: a synthesised Modern Standard Arabic voice. Audio source: Google Translate.

A QUICK CHECK

What does مَرْحَبًا mean?

A. Hello B. Thank you

Reveal the answer

A. Hello. You’ve met your first Arabic greeting.

04 / LEARNING APPROACH

See it. Hear it.
Practise it.

The proposed learning approach combines clear word examples, pronunciation demonstrations, English explanations, and short practice activities.

05 / FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

A little more clarity.

Do I need previous Arabic knowledge?

No previous knowledge is assumed in this programme concept.

Which form of Arabic does it introduce?

Modern Standard Arabic.

Can I enrol?

No. Bridge Arabic is a fictional portfolio project, and enrolment is unavailable.

Can I explore a lesson?

Yes. The greeting activity on this page demonstrates the proposed approach.
